# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — create capability from empty seed: literal-value contract + type/keep-original/delete-shift knowledge + inspect→write→verify→stop template
- Changes I made:
  - prompt.md (new) §1 grading contract. Covers formula→literal (cluster A); bool, keep-type, no serial dates, exact text copied from cells, no error markers (B/D); empty/no-placeholder (C).
  - prompt.md §2 workbook-shape rules: pre-filled targets are kept; existing formulas show the intent; emulate Excel TEXT/ROUND/case; the instruction's example format wins; row alignment; the next-row key past the target; snapshot vs overlap; "today" means the real today (C/E/F).
  - prompt.md §3 preview mapping.
  - prompt.md §4 preserve: prefer openpyxl; deleting rows/columns shifts (delete_rows/delete_cols); append conventions; don't save a data_only workbook.
  - prompt.md §5 pitfalls, including total rows and stalls.
  - task_template.md (new): all 6 placeholders plus {max_turns}; CONTRACT 1-4; Phase 1 INSPECT with calibration, Phase 2 WRITE with readback, Phase 3 VERIFY with an explicit no-code stop. This replaces the built-in "once that file exists, you are done".
- Expected effect and safety:
  - Should fix the formula cluster (56921, 59129, 59160, 45707, 11276) and the types cluster (409-45, 535-20, 45944).
  - Should fix the keep-original/overreach cluster (290-1, 469-9, 58687, 57354) and the empty-target cluster (38074).
  - Possibly fixes 203-15 and 1925 (verbatim text) and 183-8 (exclude the total row).
  - Rules are conditional, so the 16 seed passes should keep their behaviour. The rules for 28-7 (delete = shift) and 534-26 (real today) specifically target the earlier run's regressions on seed-passing tasks.
- Building on prior RESULTS:
  - No prior iteration exists in this run.
  - I used the earlier run's accepted cand_0001 (val 0.95 there, FINAL 21/40 on these val ids) as the base. Its FINAL broke 188-39, 28-7, 486-17, 50811, 52541, 534-26 and 9111; I added rules for 28-7, 534-26 and 9111.
  - I shrank its long niche sections (risk matrix, snapshot) to a line or two.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: pure logic misreadings (12307, 279-23, 304-35, 41978, 50682, 524-31, 59358, 9391). They have no shared mechanism visible without the gold files.
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration).
- Focus next iteration:
  - Read the cand_0001 val traces for the remaining logic failures and for any seed-pass regressions (watch 188-39, 486-17, 50811, 52541).
  - Prune any rule that caused over-compliance.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.600 Δ=+0.200 · fixed={11276, 304-35, 38074, 41978, 469-9, 50682, 535-20, 56921, 59160, 59358, 9391} · broke={188-39, 50521, 534-26} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.600 Δ=+0.200 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — existing-formula-cells contract + readback check; workbook-string text check; instruction-example calibration; sample-sheet/header/subset rules
- Changes I made:
  - task_template.md CONTRACT 1: formula cells already inside answer_position must end as literals. Write the cached value, or recompute it when the cache is an error or depends on changed cells. The answer_position bounds what is graded, not the instruction's narrower range (cluster A: 183-8, 524-31, 45944).
  - task_template.md Phase 2: re-open the output without data_only and print `formula cells left`; Phase 3 requires the list to be empty (A).
  - task_template.md Phase 1: compute from the data_only `ws`, because `wsf` returns formula text (45707: the `=A2+1` dates came back as strings).
  - task_template.md Phase 1: calibrate against a result value the instruction states (50521, a cand_0001 break).
  - task_template.md Phase 3: an exact-spelling check against workbook strings and quoted formula constants (1925 "NEW", 203-15); a changed-vs-`was:` justification check (57354).
  - prompt.md §2: a sample-output-sheet rule — layout from the sample, data-dependent cutoffs recomputed from today, and its own filled cells kept when answer_position is on it (409-45, 534-26).
  - prompt.md §2: a header-defines-content rule (188-39).
  - prompt.md §2: an instruction-named-subset rule (12307).
- Expected effect and safety:
  - Up to +10 tasks; realistically +4 to +6.
  - Protected tasks with formula targets (11276, 52541, 56921) already wrote literals, so the check prints an empty list for them.
  - I scripted a check over all 24 protected tasks: none has golden text that differs from a workbook string only by case or spacing.
  - 547-43 (answer_position on its Expected sheet) is protected by the "keep its filled cells" clause.
- Building on prior RESULTS:
  - cand_0001 broke 188-39, 50521 and 534-26. Each now gets a targeted edit (E8, E4, E7).
  - Nothing from cand_0001 was removed, since it was ACCEPTED with no refuted edit.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked:
  - 290-1 (pattern continuation; stalls through 30 rounds).
  - 58687, 59129, 279-23 (distinct logic errors).
- Plateau signal: none (+0.200 last iteration).
- Focus next iteration:
  - Check whether E2's readback list was printed and acted on in 183-8 and 524-31.
  - If 534-26 or 547-43 regress, narrow the sample-sheet rule.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.550 Δ=-0.050 · fixed={290-1, 50521, 59129} · broke={11276, 304-35, 38074, 51680, 59358} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them). — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
